name: Dudigital Global Limited
sector: Visa/consular outsourcing, verification and mobility services
summary: Conditional hold, not an earnings-growth bargain. DU Global has operating visa/consular and verification businesses, but headline FY2026 PAT growth is heavily affected by lower tax and noncore income. Old receivables, illiquid investments and platform cash demands dominate the investment case. Full annual funding models are complete; BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS remain NS for material economic-growth and realization inputs, with supported partial factors. No misconduct, default or critical accounting failure is inferred solely from an auditor emphasis paragraph. [S1][S5][S6][S9]
identity_note: Primary annuals and April allotment identify DUGLOBAL, ISIN INE0HPK01020; no unverified legal rename from website branding.
score_note: NS aggregates; supported partial factors and exact non-reweighted bounds. Persistent CAP/CASH weakness limits any fully scored GQS to 5.

GOV.reason: Historical loan-compliance issue and material tax dispute are disclosed with corrective/company positions. Connected disposals, continuing RPTs and unclear recovery/deployment warrant caution, not a finding of abuse. Current professional-tax/PF delays were not reported older than six months.

MOAT.reason: Government relationships, compliance infrastructure and operating centers are meaningful credentials, but tenders, price competition, short-notice arrangements and concentrated mission clients limit proven pricing power.

REV.reason: Pandemic denominator and documented gross-versus-retained visa cost change produce materially different growth bands. Three-year reported 13.6% versus direct-cost-net proxy about 37.3%; no defensible single economic-growth band without a scope/retained-fee bridge.

DUR.reason: Digitization, verification, recruitment and existing centers offer runway. Kuwait interim status and unproven platform commercialization constrain funded persistence; no perpetual contract assumed.

CAP.reason: Low normalized operating earnings relative to the large operating-asset base, negative multi-year free cash and substantial platform investment show weak realized reinvestment productivity. FY2026 after-rent EBIT proxy is about 2.24 crore before tax, not headline group PAT capitalized as operating return.

CASH.reason: Three-year CFO is -20.5603 crore, and the latest positive 8.4802 depends materially on 11.23 crore other-current-asset release. Material old receivables and investment-heavy spending prevent strong owner-cash credit.

BAL.reason: Large equity capital and some deposits support resilience, but private funds/loans are not freely available cash, 5 crore debt had a near-term maturity and possible tax/collection stresses are large. No verified current default is inferred.

EXEC.reason: Operating footprint and Kuwait commencement show delivery, but parent profit decline, substantial aged debtors and platform reinvestment without verified returns temper execution credit.

EARN.reason: Core operating profit exists, but tax-rate decline and FX/noncore income explain much of headline PAT growth. Compensation and recurring lease cash are retained in normalized models.

L.reason: Even observed-day median capacity exceeds 20 days at 5% participation; one latest trade and PAN concentration/expired market-making further constrain a 2500-share lot. Missing days are not assigned zero.

R.reason: Complete annual funding and terminal models expose downside, but recovery of auditor-emphasized receivables, private-fund realization, continuing group scope and platform/JV funding remain material low-confidence inputs. NS is not based merely on absent calibrated probabilities.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Conditional hold, not an earnings-growth bargain. DU Global has operating visa/consular and verification businesses, but headline FY2026 PAT growth is heavily affected by lower tax and noncore income. Old receivables, illiquid investments and platform cash demands dominate the investment case. Full annual funding models are complete; BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS remain NS for material economic-growth and realization inputs, with supported partial factors. No misconduct, default or critical accounting failure is inferred solely from an auditor emphasis paragraph. [S1][S5][S6][S9]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Dudigital Global Limited, NSE SME DUGLOBAL, ISIN INE0HPK01020, incorporated December 27, 2007 and listed August 26, 2021. Website branding uses DU Global Technologies; reviewed signed 2026 filings retain Dudigital Global Limited, so no unverified legal rename is assumed. Cutoff October 20, 2026; five-year horizon, 15% nominal pretax hurdle and ₹5 lakh reference position. Official October 19 price ₹23; current April-confirmed shares 71,941,741 and 2500-share lot, worth ₹57,500. Consolidated group is the analytical base, with explicit proposed-disposal and minority sensitivities. All four gates are Conditional; weakest material confidence is low for recovery, scope completion and future funding. [S1][S4][S11][S15][S17]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Partial scores: GOV 4, MOAT 4, DUR 5, CAP 3, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 4, EARN 4 and L 1; REV and R/D/P are NS. BQS coverage 88%, raw bounds 3.52–4.60; GQS coverage 60%, raw bounds 2.75–6.35. Persistent CAP/CASH weakness imposes a maximum GQS of 5 if it becomes fully scoreable; missing factors remain NS rather than reweighted. IAS coverage is 10%, bounded 1.00–9.10. No demonstrated G1/G3 failure, critical G2 hold or proven untradeability is asserted. Arithmetic and evidence are in the audit tabs. [S1][S2][S3][S15]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The group provides outsourced visa, consular and passport assistance, verification technology, travel-related services and recruitment. Government/mission contracts and actual application volumes determine revenues; market size alone is not an order book. Management reports 1.8 million-plus applications, 35 service locations, seven countries, four government/mission clients and 150 employees. FY2026 service revenue was ₹51.2356 crore plus ₹3.4369 crore other operating support services. The original IPO raised ₹4.485 crore gross, including market-maker shares, for WC, UAE subsidiary investment and general purposes. Later capital raising, not retained profit alone, funded much of the enlarged balance sheet. [S1][S3][S5]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Visa-center credentials, security processes and governmental relationships can create entry hurdles. However, larger established operators compete for sovereign tenders, low-price selection can reset economics, and electronic visas may bypass physical centers. The prospectus describes short-duration/service-provider termination risk and historical visa fees substantially remitted to a partner. DuVerify can be complementary, but capitalized software is not proof of adoption or pricing power. Concentration in a few government/mission clients and a retendered Kuwait mandate limit MOAT to 4. [S1][S5][S8][S9]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue was ₹36.7414 crore in FY2019, ₹31.5064 crore FY2020, ₹2.1785 crore pandemic FY2021, ₹9.3981 crore FY2022, then ₹37.2827/29.2502/48.1586/54.6725 crore in FY2023–26. A five-year CAGR from the pandemic trough is misleading. Three-year reported growth is about 13.6%, while a simple direct-visa-cost-net proxy grows about 37.3%; the difference is economically material, not just missing organic disclosure. FY2026 group revenue growth 13.5% contrasts with parent 6.3%. Overseas subsidiaries, salary-heavy delivery and support-service mix need a retained-fee bridge before assigning REV. The proposed OSC disposal removes ₹2.6217 crore of old revenue if completed; no newly formed DG AG turnover is invented. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Growth requires receivable collection and productive deployment, not merely more centers. Actual operating WC of ₹49.6736 crore and operating fixed/intangible/capital-advance assets of ₹23.6798 crore support only modest normalized earnings. Development assets rose to ₹10.935 crore, alongside an unexplained-target ₹5.7989 crore investment advance. After-rent cash EBITDA proxy is ₹4.7834 crore; subtracting nonlease DA gives roughly ₹2.24 crore EBIT before tax. This is weak realized reinvestment productivity. The model separately funds additional completion and optional JV support without charging already-spent assets twice. Broad ₹125 crore investment/loan authority and borrowing approvals are not actual funded commitments. [S1][S6][S7][S13]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The promoter group declared 38,832,860 shares and no encumbrance made during FY2026; this is March evidence, not October pledge clearance. The 2021 prospectus disclosed past related-director loan compliance issues under Sections 185/186, repayment with interest and later approval/filing. Current CARO reports professional-tax/PF delays but no undisputed amount older than six months. September 1 proposes selling OSC and Worldwide to promoter Rajinder Rai for ₹10.49 lakh and ₹1 lakh; the issuer calls the terms arm’s-length, but independent valuation and completed liability release are not verified. Continuing OSC RPT authority of ₹10 crore warrants margin scrutiny after any disposal. September voting and auditor replacement at the end of the old term are procedural facts, not assurance of recovery. CEO remuneration ₹1.4149 crore is material relative to owner PAT ₹5.7614 crore. [S1][S5][S6][S13][S14]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY2026 core EBIT/EBITDA are ₹3.1559/7.4962 crore, excluding ₹5.2728 crore other income including ₹3.3185 crore FX gain. PBT grew 15.3% while group PAT grew 77.1%, largely because tax expense declined; parent PAT fell 20.2%. CFO for FY2023–26 was ₹0.9289, −₹10.8876, −₹18.1529 and ₹8.4802 crore. Latest positive CFO benefited from ₹11.23 crore other-current-asset release, while cash capex was ₹16.7747 crore. Cash totals reconcile, but the cash FX line equals total foreign-operation translation OCI and needs an asset-specific bridge. Receivables ₹40.8314 crore include ₹18.5073 crore aged one to two years; auditor emphasis identifies ₹30.5257 crore foreign balances dependent on collection, without modifying the opinion. Allowance-note versus ECL-expense presentation also needs a reconciliation. These are material realization questions, not proof of missing cash or fraud. ₹21.6048 crore warrant forfeiture went to capital reserve, not operating profit or new cash. [S1][S2][S3][S19]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Official ₹23 implies capitalization ₹165.47 crore, owner-PAT P/E 28.72 and owner-book P/B 1.60. Full FY2027–31 models use actual opening WC, after-rent cash earnings, capex, tax and circular half-year debt interest. Bear/base/bull growth is −5%/12%/25%, after-rent EBITDA margin 6%/12%/18%, and exit multiple 5×/8×/11×. Private investments, loans, deposits and investment advances have separate recovery assumptions, never treated automatically as opening cash. Model per-share terminal values are ₹0.00/₹12.03/₹44.24, annual returns -100.0%/-12.2%/14.0%. They are sensitivities, not targets. Debt/equity, WC, scope and private-fund recovery variations are fully annual, with matching dilution. IAS is NS for material current recovery/scope/funding uncertainty, not simply unknown probabilities. [S1][S6][S7][S11][S15]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A collection shock can consume capital far faster than reported profits replenish it. The severe full annual model impairs 50% of the auditor-emphasized foreign-receivable balance, contracts revenue 15% yearly, funds 100% revenue WC, uses 3% after-rent margin, reduces private-asset recovery and tests payment of the disclosed ₹11.3137 crore total contingent tax amount. Impairments are noncash earnings charges/addbacks; receipt replacement funding appears once through delta WC. Tax payment is a stress, not a final adjudicated liability. The proposed sale of two subsidiaries does not automatically discharge prior guarantees. The ₹5 crore May-maturity loan requires actual repayment/rollover verification. Even the observed-day median turnover implies more than 20 days at 5% participation; latest one-trade liquidity can magnify permanent-loss risk. Counterevidence is disclosed equity capital, real operations and possible debtor/fund recovery. [S1][S6][S15]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× requires 37.97% annual per-share appreciation and ₹115 terminal value; 10× requires 58.49% and ₹230. The already demanding bull case reaches ₹44.24, about 1.92× current price, before claiming any undisclosed large mandate. Faster revenue growth alone would worsen funding unless WC falls and platform returns emerge. Expired warrants are not an additional financing pool. Neither historical pandemic-recovery CAGR nor a large capital reserve supports a 5×/10× label. [S1][S5][S11][S15]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Verify collection of the ₹30.5257 crore flagged foreign balances, the one-to-two-year debtor bucket, unbilled conversions and entity-level ECL/FX reconciliation. Confirm repayment or rollover of the ₹5 crore May-maturity loan, investment-fund liquidity and target/use of the ₹5.7989 crore advance. Obtain completion and guarantee-release terms for proposed promoter disposals, final DG AG funding/ownership and current Kuwait tender outcome. Track new platform cash receipts against capitalized costs, not application counts alone. Refresh tax-dispute status without assuming an adverse outcome. Monitor after-rent margins, current shares/options, current encumbrances, dated restrictions and live depth. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S9][S11][S15][S16]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Deep research is complete at an explicit conditional hold: a real operating business, but not currently a demonstrated quality compounder or decision-grade attractive investment. Partial factors and bounds are retained; aggregate scores are NS. Full linked annual models are provided rather than unperformed valuation work being relabeled as a data hold. No default, fraud, suspension or court finding is invented. The historical compliance, tax and tender passages retain their dated sources and stated qualifications. This research does not execute a trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary FY2022/24/25/26 annuals, final prospectus and April–October signed filings support this review. The old FY2025 website URL failed; the current official archive supplied the report and its core numbers agree with FY2026 comparatives. The June reupload was compared, not assumed to correct all presentation issues. Later July 23 Kuwait interim operations explicitly supersede an interpretation based only on the July 16 judgment disclosure. Directory/cutoff searches did not verify final tender renewal, disposal completion, funding or subsequent tax disposition; absence of a located update is not proof none exists. Future margins, growth, recoveries, FX conversion and funding are analyst assumptions. Official market data are dated; eight absent sessions are not silently zero-filled. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9][S15][S16][S18][S19]

valuation.status: Full conditional five-year cash-rental operating model and asset/funding bridge; not a price target
valuation.units: INR crore except share count and per-share rupees
valuation.opening_WC_formula: 40.8314 receivables + 0.4932 noncurrent security + 0.0594 noncurrent prepaids + 3.6474 current security + 0.0257 other financial receivable + 3.9891 unbilled + 5.0641 other current assets - 0.5569 payables - 1.3636 employee payable - 1.8036 other current liabilities - 0.7126 provisions = 49.6736
methodology: Actual March opening balances are used. Current April allotment cash 0.0139576 is included separately in the final cash bridge. A full-year 2.6217 revenue carve-out is conditional on the proposed OSC disposal; alternative full-group scenarios preserve it. No unverified disposal proceeds, derecognition gain, loan release or guarantee discharge is assumed.

Historical EBITDA 7.4962 excludes other income, including 3.3185 FX gain. Subtracting historical lease principal 2.2778 plus lease interest 0.4350 gives after-rent cash EBITDA proxy 4.7834. Forecast margins are after replacement cash rent and compensation; no lease debt is then subtracted from terminal after-rent EV. Nonlease depreciation is forecast at 4.5% of revenue. Existing ROU assets/lease debt are not a second asset/cash charge.

ESOP expense is not added back to forecast earnings; modeled margins assume cash-equivalent compensation. Remaining INR 2 options 371715 are exercised with matching cash/shares in FY2027. INR 25 strike options 31280 are separately sensitized. Expired 17,283,840 warrants and already forfeited 21.6048 crore are not future funding or dilution.

Other investments 21.0484, loans 4.9676, investment advance 5.7989 and retained deposits are not free cash. Explicit principal recoveries reduce terminal balances. Investment funds are valued at terminal recovery fractions without assumed recurring return. Actual investment advance has no verified target economics; no invented earnings are added.

Additional platform completion and JV growth cash are analyst sensitivities, not disclosed committed budgets. Already spent IAUD 10.9350 and capital advances 2.6300 are not charged again. The USD 5100 planned DG AG acquisition is translated at assumed INR 95/USD, 0.04845 crore, once; no new-company revenue is fabricated.
